The bug is fixed: `![x\"x](x)` with `-x smarty` now gives `

`, the same as the unescaped version. Nothing is committed. **Cause:** a backslash-escaped character is stored as a placeholder during parsing. The old `UnescapePostprocessor` turned it back into the real character only after the HTML had already been written out as text. So the serializer never saw the `"` and never escaped it inside the attribute. Smarty makes `"` and `'` escapable, which is how a raw `"` got into `alt="…"`. **Fix** (this follows the approach upstream Python-Markdown took for this issue in 3.4): - `markdown/treeprocessors.py`: a new `UnescapeTreeprocessor`, registered as `unescape` at priority 0. It restores escaped characters in element text, tails and attribute values before the HTML is written out, so the serializer escapes them properly. It skips the text of `` elements, as upstream does. - `markdown/postprocessors.py`: `UnescapePostprocessor` is no longer registered by default. It still works if called directly, but now raises a `DeprecationWarning`. I put the warning in `__init__` rather than wrapping the class, so code that subclasses it keeps working. - `markdown/extensions/toc.py`: its `unescape()` helper now uses the new tree processor, so it doesn't trigger the warning. **Visible side effect:** escaped characters in normal text now get the usual HTML escaping, so `\>` renders as `>` instead of `>`. That is valid HTML, and upstream changed the same expected output, so I updated `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` to match. Third-party extensions that removed the `unescape` postprocessor by name, or put escape placeholders into stored raw HTML, would be affected. I noted this in `docs/change_log/release-3.4.md`. **Tests:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` covers escaped quotes in text, image alt text (inline and reference style), link titles and code spans. Three of these fail on the original code and pass now. - `tests/test_apis.py` checks the deprecation warning and confirms `unescape` is now a tree processor rather than a postprocessor. - I also updated the processor tables in `docs/extensions/api.md`. **Test results:** 981 tests run with `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover tests`, with 8 failures. All 8 also fail on the untouched code; they're the HTML-block tests for unclosed tags and comments, in `test_html_blocks` and `test_md_in_html`. Running the full suite through `pytest` stops before any tests run, because `test_md_in_html.py` has a `TestSuite` class pytest can't collect. That also happens on the untouched code.
